notes: TBox, as geography-replace-0005. 'One path separator per system' is a firm rule (the questions ask 'which character'). Linux's membership and its stored separator are separate background facts; each world gives up one.

queries.not_checked: the gold paths docs/notes.txt and docs\notes.txt differ only in punctuation, which surface matching ignores, so they cannot be told apart as answers

fol.notes: Only for q1, which is labelled dl and has no checker: its two gold paths, docs/notes.txt and docs\notes.txt, differ only in punctuation, which the DL check's surface matching ignores. Here the path is a String (rel_path, local) built by a firm rule from the system's separator character (sep_char, local), and fol_check reads String answers verbatim, so the two are told apart. Systems are an uninterpreted sort; uses_path_separator is a function to an enumeration of separators (the DL file's firm one_separator). Linux's membership and its stored separator are separate facts, each given up by one world, as in the DL file (q1 does not use them). fol_check.py only checks queries labelled fol and rejects a fol-section entry for a dl query, so q1 is not listed under queries; the entry it would take is {"q": 1, "given": {"tessaly_member": {"says": "Tessaly OS is a Unix-like operating system.", "z3": "unix_like(tessaly)"}}, "find": "rel_path(tessaly)"}, which gives docs/notes.txt before the edit (core: given, sep_chars, path_rule, original) and docs\notes.txt after it in both worlds (core: given, sep_chars, path_rule, edit), checked outside the report.

local.sep_char: sep_char(s): the character separator s is written as ('/', '\')
local.rel_path: rel_path(o): the relative path of the file notes.txt inside the directory docs on system o

sep_chars.says: The forward slash is written '/', the backslash '\'.

path_rule.says: On a system, the relative path of notes.txt inside docs joins the directory and the file name with the system's separator.

linux_member.says: Linux is a Unix-like operating system. (stored)

linux_stored.says: Linux uses the forward slash (/) as its path separator. (stored)

label_corrections.why: Not because DL can't express the rule (the DL file has a firm path rule to named path individuals), but because the two gold answers are strings that differ only in the separator: only a string-valued check (Z3 String theory, answers read verbatim) can tell docs/notes.txt from docs\notes.txt.
